question: In a citywide collection program, what does a sewershed level performance dashboard most usefully give senior managers?
correctAnswer: A basin by basin view of flows, defects, overflows and costs that shows where attention is needed
explanation: A basin level dashboard puts flows, condition and cost side by side, which shows managers where problems concentrate and where spending will do the most good.
options: A single ranking of crews by hours worked and overtime claimed in each district each month
A basin by basin view of flows, defects, overflows and costs that shows where attention is needed
A replacement for field inspection, flow monitoring and condition assessment across the system
A list of every pipe ranked only by installation year, from the oldest main in the city to the newest subdivision
optionA: A single ranking of crews by hours worked and overtime claimed in each district each month
optionB: A basin by basin view of flows, defects, overflows and costs that shows where attention is needed
optionC: A replacement for field inspection, flow monitoring and condition assessment across the system
optionD: A list of every pipe ranked only by installation year, from the oldest main in the city to the newest subdivision
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: What are the four core elements that give the CMOM approach its name?
correctAnswer: Capacity, management, operations and maintenance
explanation: CMOM stands for capacity, management, operations and maintenance, the four program areas a utility organizes to control overflows and run the system well.
options: Capacity, management, operations and maintenance
Collection, metering, odour control and marketing
Contracts, materials, overtime and manuals
Capacity, manpower, overtime and monitoring
optionA: Capacity, management, operations and maintenance
optionB: Collection, metering, odour control and marketing
optionC: Contracts, materials, overtime and manuals
optionD: Capacity, manpower, overtime and monitoring

question: What is normally the first phase of a well designed infiltration and inflow reduction program?
correctAnswer: Measuring and locating the I&I so work targets the sources that matter most
explanation: Finding and quantifying the sources comes first, because rehabilitation money spent without flow and defect data often treats pipes that contribute little I&I.
options: Rehabilitating every main in the oldest neighbourhood first, whether or not its flows are high
Buying lining equipment and hiring extra crews so construction can start in the first month
Measuring and locating the I&I so work targets the sources that matter most
Raising sewer rates across the city to fund a larger construction budget for later program years

optionB: Buying lining equipment and hiring extra crews so construction can start in the first month
optionC: Measuring and locating the I&I so work targets the sources that matter most
optionD: Raising sewer rates across the city to fund a larger construction budget for later program years

question: In rainfall dependent infiltration and inflow analysis, what does the R value represent?
correctAnswer: The ratio of rainfall volume that enters the sewer as RDII
explanation: The R value is the fraction of rainfall volume over the tributary area that shows up in the sewer as rainfall dependent infiltration and inflow.
options: The roughness coefficient of the sewer pipe wall
The ratio of rainfall volume that enters the sewer as RDII
The return period of the design storm in years
The reserve capacity held at the treatment plant
optionA: The roughness coefficient of the sewer pipe wall
optionB: The ratio of rainfall volume that enters the sewer as RDII
optionC: The return period of the design storm in years
optionD: The reserve capacity held at the treatment plant

question: Across a network of many lift stations, what is the main benefit of standardizing pump models and control panels?
correctAnswer: Spare parts, training and troubleshooting become simpler and faster across the whole system
explanation: Common pumps and panels mean one parts inventory, one training standard and faster repairs, which matters when dozens of stations must be kept running.
options: Stations can be left unvisited for much longer periods between routine operator rounds each week
Every station in the network can be operated safely without any standby power supply
Spare parts, training and troubleshooting become simpler and faster across the whole system
Wet wells at standardized stations no longer need high level alarms or backup controls

question: What is the purpose of an air release valve at a high point on a sewage force main?
correctAnswer: To let accumulated air escape so it does not restrict flow or add head
explanation: Air collects at high points and can block flow and raise pumping head, so air release valves vent it from the force main.
options: To let accumulated air escape so it does not restrict flow or add head
To release sewage safely to grade through a bypass during a pump failure event
To measure the flow rate and pressure in the force main at its highest point
To mix fresh air into the sewage so odours are controlled along the force main
optionA: To let accumulated air escape so it does not restrict flow or add head
optionB: To release sewage safely to grade through a bypass during a pump failure event
optionC: To measure the flow rate and pressure in the force main at its highest point
optionD: To mix fresh air into the sewage so odours are controlled along the force main
sourceTitle: US EPA - Alternative Wastewater Collection Systems Manual

question: Hydrogen sulfide damage in a collection system most often attacks which part of a sewer?
correctAnswer: The crown and upper walls above the waterline, where acid forms on moist surfaces
explanation: Sulfide released from the flow forms acid on moist crown surfaces above the waterline, and that acid attacks concrete and metal there.
options: The submerged invert where the flow runs deepest and fastest during dry weather periods
The crown and upper walls above the waterline, where acid forms on moist surfaces
The outside of the pipe where it sits buried in dry, well drained soil beside the trench
The maintenance hole benching below the channel where wastewater ponds after each storm
optionA: The submerged invert where the flow runs deepest and fastest during dry weather periods
optionB: The crown and upper walls above the waterline, where acid forms on moist surfaces
optionC: The outside of the pipe where it sits buried in dry, well drained soil beside the trench
optionD: The maintenance hole benching below the channel where wastewater ponds after each storm
sourceTitle: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety - Hydrogen Sulfide

question: In a fats, oils and grease program, what is the role of a grease interceptor at a food service establishment?
correctAnswer: To slow the flow so FOG can separate and be held for removal before it reaches the sewer
explanation: An interceptor holds the flow long enough for grease to float and solids to settle, so FOG is captured at the source and pumped out on a schedule.
options: To grind food waste and suspended solids so they pass quickly through the downstream sewer
To cool the wastewater and settle grit before it reaches the municipal treatment plant
To dose enzymes into the flow that dissolve grease as it travels through the downstream main
To slow the flow so FOG can separate and be held for removal before it reaches the sewer

optionB: To cool the wastewater and settle grit before it reaches the municipal treatment plant
optionC: To dose enzymes into the flow that dissolve grease as it travels through the downstream main
optionD: To slow the flow so FOG can separate and be held for removal before it reaches the sewer

Direct study and rehabilitation funds to the three problem sewersheds while routine care continues elsewhere
Replace the largest trunk sewer in the system first, since it carries flow from every sewershed
Add permanent flow monitors at the treatment plant inlet and wait for the pattern to change on its own

question: Flow monitoring shows one basin contributes a large share of wet weather flow but smoke testing there finds few defects. What is the best next step in the I&I program?
correctAnswer: Investigate other entry paths in that basin, such as maintenance hole covers, cross connections and private laterals
explanation: When one test finds little, the program checks the other known entry paths in the same basin rather than abandoning a basin the flow data flags as wet.

Investigate other entry paths in that basin, such as maintenance hole covers, cross connections and private laterals
Repeat the same smoke test in the same streets each season until visible defects finally appear
Line the longest main in the basin right away without any further study of where the wet weather flow actually enters

explanation: Splitting the response into fast, medium and slow parts estimates how the RDII volume is spread over time, which drives the predicted peak and its timing.

The exact pipe that leaked during the storm and the joint where the water entered it
The chlorine demand and disinfection load arriving at the treatment plant that day
The pump run times and wet well levels recorded at each lift station in the sewershed during the storm

question: A trunk sewer downstream of a long force main discharge has repeated odour complaints and visible crown corrosion. What is the most likely underlying cause?
correctAnswer: Sulfide built up during long detention in the force main, released as hydrogen sulfide at the discharge
explanation: Long force main detention lets sewage turn septic and build sulfide, which is released at the turbulent discharge and drives odour and crown corrosion downstream.
options: Cold groundwater entering slowly through leaking pipe joints along the long gravity sewer reach upstream
Sulfide built up during long detention in the force main, released as hydrogen sulfide at the discharge
Excess dissolved oxygen carried in the gravity sewer flow from an upstream aerated process discharge
Sand and grit that settled along the sewer invert during the low overnight flow period last week
optionA: Cold groundwater entering slowly through leaking pipe joints along the long gravity sewer reach upstream
optionB: Sulfide built up during long detention in the force main, released as hydrogen sulfide at the discharge
optionC: Excess dissolved oxygen carried in the gravity sewer flow from an upstream aerated process discharge
optionD: Sand and grit that settled along the sewer invert during the low overnight flow period last week
sourceTitle: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety - Hydrogen Sulfide

correctAnswer: Inventory and inspect the establishments, then bring missing or undersized interceptors into the inspection program
explanation: The program cannot manage establishments it has not inventoried, so inspection and records come before enforcement or sizing corrections.

Inventory and inspect the establishments, then bring missing or undersized interceptors into the inspection program
Fine every establishment on the strip immediately, including the ones that already have proper working interceptors installed and records
Reduce the sewer use charges for the whole restaurant strip until the blockages stop occurring on their own
